# Three genuine CM-point Frobenius entries from the Hasse derivative

2026-10-15. Separate bounded paper unit, original owner
EM-DIRECT-18F24A and support EM-CM24CONN-63E74C9D. Root
EM-DVR-FBF223 supplied the three-entry method and is a real
coauthor, not a decisive independent reviewer. This proof uses no
unknown target value, program, prime instance or new source search.

**Conditional status:** the fixed degree-six CM package remains
under distinct review. Its exact CM shape, cup normalization and
Hodge divisibility are hypotheses in the three-entry conclusion
below, not a prematurely inherited PASS. The Hasse normalization
and ambient horizontal calculation are proved separately here.
The degree-six and all earlier frozen originals are unchanged.

The input candidate is
`control/ROOT_CM24_CM_POINT_FROBENIUS_HOL0MORPHIC_COLUMN_MOD_P2_CANDIDATE_20261015.md`
(HOL0 contains the digit zero). This proof concerns only the true
sigma-Frobenius first column and its second diagonal entry modulo
p². It does not determine the remaining unit entry modulo p².

## Actual family, matrices and normalization

Let p=6m+1≡13,19mod24, n=2m. Use the already bound actual family

    E_t:y²=f_t(x)=x³+(12t−15)x+4t²−28t+22,
    omega=dx/(2y), eta=x dx/(2y), e=(omega,eta).

The coefficient ring is the good-locus dagger ring over Z_p with
t and(1−t²)^(-1); all differentiations below are ambient relative
parameter derivatives. The integral proper cohomology basis and
its constant cup normalization are those in the frozen geometric
proof: under a fixed residue convention <omega,eta>=1. In particular
the image v of eta in H¹(O_E)=H¹_dR/Fil¹ is Serre dual to omega
with pairing1, and the same convention holds on every source fibre.

Write M_phi(t) for the GENUINE class-column Frobenius pullback
matrix from phi(t)=t^p to t, in these Weierstrass bases. The prior
MW construction/precision proof supplies the actual integral
relative Frobenius structure; a determinant-p or chosen-initial-value
comparison alone would not be enough. On the reduction modulo p it
is induced by the relative Frobenius E_t->E_(t^p).

At the halfpoint t=zeta, take O=W(Fp²), zeta²=1/2 and the actual
coefficient automorphism sigma(zeta)=−zeta. M_sigma denotes the
corresponding pullback from sigma(e_zeta) to e_zeta, not a matrix
for a Frobenius self-map of the displayed curve and not a period
dual/inverse normalization. Raw zeta^p and sigma(zeta) agree
modulo p, although they need not agree modulo p².

## Positive Hasse quotient scalar, with the relative Cartier convention

Let l=(p−1)/2 and define the polynomial

    h(t)=[x^(p−1)] f_t(x)^l in Fp[t].                (1)

The relative Cartier operator here has source differentials on E_t
and target differentials on its relative Frobenius twist E_(t^p).
It is linear over the parameter base, with target differential dx'
and target coordinate y'. On the chart where y is invertible,

    omega=f_t(x)^l dx/(2y^p).

Use C_rel(F_rel^*g *xi)=g C_rel(xi). The monomial rule selects
powers x^j dx with j congruent p−1 modulo p, sending x^(p−1)dx
to dx'. Since deg_x f_t^l=3(p−1)/2<2p−1, only j=p−1 survives.
Consequently, as an equality of holomorphic differentials,

    C_rel(omega_t)=h(t) omega_(t^p).                 (2)

There is NO p-th root of h in(2). An absolute Cartier operator
made semilinear on a single perfect-field curve can be described
using such a root; it is not the relative source/target convention
of M_phi. Equation(2) first holds on the dense chart and hence
extends globally. The factor2 has no hidden effect: its inverse
is a base constant and p is odd.

To see the sign and quotient basis explicitly, represent a class
of H¹(O) by a Čech principal part g. Relative Serre duality obeys

    <omega_t, F_O(g_(t^p))>_t
        =<C_rel(omega_t),g_(t^p)>_(t^p).             (3)

This can be verified locally by residues: pulling a principal
part back replaces its local coordinate by its p-th power; the
coefficient of the resulting residue is exactly the one selected
by the relative Cartier monomial rule. Thus there is no negative
sign in(3). Applying(3) to the fixed dual quotient generator v
and using(2) gives

    F_O(v_(t^p))=h(t)v_t.                            (4)

Relative Frobenius pulls every holomorphic differential to zero
modulo p. Combining this with(4), in the SAME integral proper
cohomology basis, gives

    M_phi,11=M_phi,21=0 modp,
    M_phi,22=h(t) modp.                              (5)

The second equality is a quotient/Hasse statement, not a finite-field
trace assertion at a nonsplit halfpoint. It uses the positive,
constant Serre-dual basis scalar; arbitrarily scaling eta independently
on the two fibres would change the matrix statement.

The source-bound variable identity from Sun Corollary3.1 gives
`P_floor(p/3)(t)=(p/3)h(t)` modulo p. Here(p/3)=1, so

    h(t)=P_n(t), n=2m.                               (6)

This reuses the frozen curve/Hasse binding, without reopening or
reclassifying its literature. It is valid in Fp[t] and may be
evaluated in Fp². No character sum over Fp is called the trace of
E_zeta, whose displayed coefficients generally lie in Fp².

## Ambient horizontality determines the remaining mod-p unit

The actual class connection is nabla e=e C(t), with

    C=[[alpha,gamma],[beta_c,−alpha]],
    alpha=−(2t−1)/[6(t²−1)],
    beta_c=−1/[6(t²−1)],
    gamma=−(4t−5)/[6(t²−1)].

For the columns-of-pullbacks convention, genuine horizontality is

    M_phi'=phi' M_phi C(phi(t))−C(t)M_phi.             (7)

Reduce(7) modulo p BEFORE evaluation: phi'=p t^(p−1) vanishes,
while parameter derivation preserves the integral dagger lattice.
The second-row/second-column equation, using(5), is

    h'=−beta_c *M_phi,12+alpha*h modp.                (8)

The known source halfpoint has h(zeta)=P_n(zeta)=0. Also
beta_c(zeta)=1/3. Hence

    M_phi,12(zeta)=−3h'(zeta) modp.                   (9)

This is the ambient derivative of the polynomial(6); no derivative
of zeta²=1/2, a specialized point matrix, or a point-only Taylor
identity was taken. The scalar3 comes from the actual GM basis,
not from an additional elliptic isogeny or target-dependent fit.

## Conditional CM input and three mod-p² entries

Assume precisely the degree-six package's fixed CM conclusions,
pending its distinct review. In canonical sigma-source Weierstrass
bases they state

    M_sigma=[[ (zeta−1)C_0, B+(zeta²−1)C_0 ],
               [ C_0,        (zeta+1)C_0 ]],
    B*C_0=−p, B in O^*, C_0 in pO.                 (10)

The symbol C_0 here is a scalar entry, not the connection matrix
C(t). It is the genuine undivided crystalline Frobenius shape
in a proper integral lattice. In particular its determinant and
divisibility are not being guessed from a transport ansatz.

The comparison between phi(zeta)=zeta^p and sigma(zeta)=−zeta
is p-small and reduces to the identity on the displayed bases.
For(9) we need ONLY this modulo-p identity; no choice of its
mod-p² Taylor sign is needed. Thus M_phi(zeta)=M_sigma modp.
In particular the zero h(zeta) used above also follows under these
conditional hypotheses directly from(5) and the p-divisible lower
diagonal entry in(10); the main conditional result does not require
an additional unverified root-value assumption.
Since C_0 is p-divisible, equations(9)–(10) imply

    B=−3h'(zeta) modp.                               (11)

Because B is a unit, h'(zeta) is nonzero in Fp². Thus the needed
unit denominator follows within these conditional hypotheses;
the old simple-root argument could also be reused but is not
reproved or counted as new information here.

Choose ANY integral lift u in O of h'(zeta). Then(10)–(11) give

    C_0=−p/B = p/(3u) modp²,
    M_sigma,21=p/(3u) modp²,
    M_sigma,11=p(zeta−1)/(3u) modp²,
    M_sigma,22=p(zeta+1)/(3u) modp².                 (12)

The sign is positive: B reduces to−3u and C_0=−p/B. Replacing
u by u+pz changes p/(3u) by a multiple of p², so all three
entries are independent of the chosen lift. They are therefore
well-defined expressions in only the already specified polynomial
derivative modulo p and the fixed halfpoint coefficient lift.

The remaining entry has only the value

    M_sigma,12=−3h'(zeta) modp.                      (13)

Its p-correction is not fixed by this argument. Equation(10)
contains that correction both through B and through the known
p-divisible term(zeta²−1)C_0; no unspecified lift of(13) is
promoted to a mod-p² answer. Conversely that missing correction
does not affect(12), as its contribution to−p/B is already p².

## Logical scope and stopping boundary

Equations(1)–(9) establish the normalization/sign and global-family
derivative mechanism for the actual Frobenius structure. The
three-entry statement(12) is CONDITIONAL on the pending frozen
degree-six CM shape(10). No independent review of that package is
supplied by this author proof, and no unchanged old PASS is enlarged.
All uses of cohomology, quotient and Serre-dual basis share the
declared integral class-column convention. An inverse-dual or
period-solution matrix cannot be substituted without its separate
variance and basis conversion.

Even after the CM premise is independently verified, (12) gives
three matrix VALUES only. It does not determine B modulo p²,
an ambient first jet of M, a complete unit-period value, the divided
complementary R(zeta) endpoint, or a relation to the whole weighted
ell(T)=3Y functional with H_b and quarter terms. Those questions,

No scientific code, prime/sample, checker/Hart/solve, new search,

## 1. Relative Cartier normalization and the positive quotient scalar

The relative source/target convention is essential. This does not confuse relative Cartier with an absolute semilinear Cartier operator on a perfect-field fibre. Base-linearity of the former, and the fixed twist basis, are what make the displayed family scalar correct. The dense-chart calculation extends to the holomorphic differential globally.

The adjointness in (3) is also correctly oriented: relative Frobenius pulls a target H¹(O) class to the source, whereas Cartier carries a source differential to the target. In a local residue representative, pulling a principal part back replaces its coordinate by its pth power, and Cartier selects exactly the corresponding coefficient in the source differential. Under that hypothesis, the upper-right entry reduces to B. Combining with the ambient calculation gives B=−3h'(zeta) modulo p. Because B is a unit, the derivative is nonzero. This is a valid way to establish the required denominator within the conditional theorem; it does not assume a simple-root theorem that depends on the desired formulas, nor use an unknown target value or ratio to choose the sign.

## 4. Three mod-p² values and precisely what remains unknown

For any integral lift u of h'(zeta), the hypothesis and congruence give `C_0=−p/B=p/(3u)` modulo p². The sign is positive because B reduces to −3u. Multiplying by the fixed integral factors zeta−1 and zeta+1 yields the two diagonal entries in (12), with the lower-left entry already C_0. Every inverse is of the now-proved unit 3u. The chosen coefficient lift of zeta is fixed; it is not silently replaced by ambient raw power.

Replacing u by u+pz changes its inverse by a multiple of p, hence p/(3u) by a multiple of p². The three reported entries are therefore independent of this auxiliary lift. The missing p-correction to B also has no effect on them at this precision.

By contrast the upper-right entry is B+(zeta²−1)C_0. Its second summand is now known modulo p², but B itself is known only modulo p. The argument supplies no first correction of B and cannot promote (13) to an unspecified mod-p² lift. No extra entry, ambient first jet, global horizontal solution or full matrix evaluation is justified.

## Remaining scope and review boundary

The accepted local result is the generic positive Hasse quotient and derivative mechanism together with the conditional implication from (10) to (12). The degree-six premise retains its own distinct-review requirement. If it is later independently established at exactly the declared integral and semilinear conventions, this implication can be used; that later status is not assumed in this file.

Even then, the whole weighted original ell(T)=3Y remains unmatched: H_b, the quarter contribution and exact relative primitive boundaries cannot be discarded by passing to proper H¹. The divided complementary endpoint/response, complete unit period, matrix first jet, Y/Z/kappa and all mathematical parents remain OPEN. There is no new Frobenius self-map claim at the nonsplit point, efficiency theorem, universal selector or target-fitted normalization.

This was a local paper audit with ordinary text/JSON/pin custody only.
